[![Build
Status](https://github.com/OHDSI/Eunomia/workflows/R-CMD-check/badge.svg)](https://github.com/OHDSI/Eunomia/actions?query=workflow%3AR-CMD-check)

[![CRAN_Status_Badge](http://cranlogs.r-pkg.org/badges/Eunomia)](https://cran.r-project.org/package=Eunomia)

Eunomia is part of [HADES](https://ohdsi.github.io/Hades/).

# Introduction

Eunomia is a standard dataset manager for sample OMOP (Observational
Medical Outcomes Partnership) Common Data Model (CDM) datasets. Eunomia
facilitates access to sample datasets from the [EunomiaDatasets
repository](https://github.com/ohdsi/EunomiaDatasets). Eunomia is used
for testing and demonstration purposes, including many of the exercises
in [the Book of OHDSI](https://ohdsi.github.io/TheBookOfOhdsi/). For
functions that require schema name, use ‘main’.

The default dataset is GiBleed in OMOP CDM v5.5 format. Earlier
supported CDM versions remain available by setting the `cdmVersion`
argument explicitly.

# Features

- Download selected sample datasets from [EunomiaDatasets
  repository](https://github.com/ohdsi/EunomiaDatasets), which includes
  a subset of the Standardized Vocabularies.
- Interfaces with the DatabaseConnector and SqlRender packages.
- No need to set up a database server. Eunomia runs in your R instance
  (currently using SQLite).
- (planned) supports for other databases

# Example

``` r

library(Eunomia)
connectionDetails <- getEunomiaConnectionDetails()
connection <- connect(connectionDetails)
querySql(connection, "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM person;")
#  COUNT(*)
#1     2694

getTableNames(connection,databaseSchema = 'main')
disconnect(connection)
```

# Technology

Eunomia is an R package providing access to sample datasets at
[EunomiaDatasets repository](https://github.com/ohdsi/EunomiaDatasets).

# System Requirements

Requires R. Some of the packages required by Eunomia require Java.

# Installation

1.  See the instructions
    [here](https://ohdsi.github.io/Hades/rSetup.html) for configuring
    your R environment, including Java.

2.  In R, use the following commands to download and install Eunomia:

``` r

install.packages("Eunomia")
```

# Package index

## All functions

- [`createCohorts()`](https://ohdsi.github.io/Eunomia/reference/createCohorts.md)
  : Construct cohorts
- [`downloadEunomiaData()`](https://ohdsi.github.io/Eunomia/reference/downloadEunomiaData.md)
  : Download Eunomia data files
- [`exportDataFiles()`](https://ohdsi.github.io/Eunomia/reference/exportDataFiles.md)
  : Export data files from a database(sqlite or duckdb)
- [`extractLoadData()`](https://ohdsi.github.io/Eunomia/reference/extractLoadData.md)
  : Extract the Eunomia data files and load into a database Extract
  files from a .ZIP file and creates a OMOP CDM database that is then
  stored in the same directory as the .ZIP file.
- [`getDatabaseFile()`](https://ohdsi.github.io/Eunomia/reference/getDatabaseFile.md)
  : Create a copy of a Eunomia dataset
- [`getEunomiaConnectionDetails()`](https://ohdsi.github.io/Eunomia/reference/getEunomiaConnectionDetails.md)
  : Get Default Eunomia Connection Details
- [`loadDataFiles()`](https://ohdsi.github.io/Eunomia/reference/loadDataFiles.md)
  : Load data files into a database(sqlite or duckdb)
